title: Compression springs and tension springs compared
examples: What is the difference between a compression and a tension spring?
Which spring is in a pen?
Why does a trampoline use stretchy springs?

explain.say: Coil springs come in two main kinds. Both are wires wound into a helix, but one is made to be squashed and the other to be stretched.

explain.say: A compression spring has gaps between its coils. Squash it and it pushes back. It sits in a ballpoint pen's click, under mattresses and in car suspension.

explain.say: A tension spring, also called an extension spring, has its coils wound tightly together with a hook at each end. Pull it and it pulls back, like the springs round a trampoline.

explain.say: Either way, the further you squash or stretch the spring, the harder it pushes or pulls, until it reaches its elastic limit. Engineers choose the type by asking: does this part need a push or a pull?

faq.a: A compression spring is an open coil spring that resists being squashed. When you press it, it pushes back with a force that grows the more you press.
A tension spring, or extension spring, is a tightly wound coil with hooks at its ends. It resists being stretched and pulls back towards its starting length.

faq.q: Which spring is in a pen?
faq.a: A click pen uses a small compression spring. Pressing the button squashes it, and it pushes the ink tube back up when you release the catch.
asks: What spring is in a ballpoint pen?

faq.q: Why does a trampoline use tension springs?
faq.a: When you land, the mat pulls on the springs round its edge and stretches them. Their pull back throws you up into the air.

faq.q: Is there a spring that twists?
faq.a: Yes. A torsion spring resists being twisted. Clothes pegs, mousetraps and some hinges use them.

facts: Tension springs are often wound with their coils pressed together, so they need a starting pull before they stretch at all.
Clothes pegs and mousetraps use torsion springs, which resist twisting.

quiz.say: Which spring would you use in a car's suspension, which is squashed by bumps?
quiz.show: Which spring would you use in a car's suspension, which is squashed by bumps?
quiz.why: Bumps squash the suspension, so it needs a spring that pushes back when compressed.

wrong.1: Tension springs resist stretching, not squashing.
wrong.2: Without springs every bump would jolt the car.
